messages.author: 6ad178c9bfa534b7
messages.subject: Stan Syntax Highlighting for pygments, google-code-prettify, and listings
parts:
Hi, 

First, I want to thank everyone for an awesome piece of software.  I benchmarked it on some dynamic linear models and it was comparable in ESS and superior in speed to 
the forward filtering backward sampling implementation in the dlm package.

Since you are working on the webpage, I thought it might be nice to have syntax highlighting for Stan models.  So, I added Stan support for most of the popular pretty printing programs that produce HTML or LaTeX. 
  • Pygments: https://github.com/jrnold/pygments_bugs
  • google-code-prettify: https://github.com/jrnold/prettify-lang-r-bugs
  • listings LaTeX package: https://github.com/jrnold/lstBUGS
I filed issues or pull-requests for both pygments (https://bitbucket.org/birkenfeld/pygments-main/pull-request/89/bugs-like-language-lexers) and prettify (http://code.google.com/p/google-code-prettify/issues/detail?id=234), 
so maybe at some point they will be merged upstream and Stan models will be natively highlighted on github, googlecode, etc. 

The pygments implementation is by far the most complete, and produces both LaTeX and HTML. And many static site generators, like Jekyll, have pygments support built in.   As an example, I attached the LaTeX and HTML output
for the magnesium.stan example using the default pygments style. 

I really appreciate your work, and would love to be able to contribute back in any way possible.

Jeffrey Arnold
PhD candidate, Political Science, University of Rochester

messages.author: 6ad178c9bfa534b7
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] Stan Syntax Highlighting for pygments, google-code-prettify, and listings
parts:
There's a variety of ways that you can add the syntax highlighting. I attached a couple of patches and the pdf of the created manual for two of these methods. I only highlighted code chunks in Chapters 7 - 13 (whatever was in programming.tex)
  1. listings.patch and stan-reference-listings.pdf requires no external dependencies and just uses the listings package
  2. minted.patch and stan-reference-minted.pdf requires installing pygments and my package pygments_bugs. It also uses the minted LaTeX package (http://code.google.com/p/minted/), but I include that .sty file in the patch.
It would also be easy to separate out the stan files and then either use the minted package or compile the source into latex and include the files by adding a step to the makefile.  In https://github.com/jrnold/pygments_bugs/tree/master/examples/stan uses a makefile to create html files for a bunch of the stan exaples.  

Something else that you might consider is converting the manual to restructuredText. Then you can compile the same source into html for the website, and a pdf manual and not duplicate content. 

Regarding contributing, what's the best way to send contributions. I found a few typos in the manual (e.g. the example on p. 82 refers to a function rand_normal which doesn't appear to exist) and some bugs/features to add to rstan.  Should I open up an issue and attach a patch? 
 

Jeff
